questions.q: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Path are categories of:
questions.solution: These four are animation effect types acting on objects within a slide. Transitions only control slide-to-slide changeover.
questions.shortcut: Object effects = animation (the 4 categories listed); slide changeover = transition.

questions.q: In MS Excel, the shortcut Shift+F3 opens the:
questions.solution: In Excel, Shift+F3 opens Insert Function (the fx dialog). The change-case meaning belongs to MS Word, which is the trap. Name Manager is Ctrl+F3.
questions.shortcut: Same key, different app: Word = case, Excel = function.

questions.q: Which of the following is regarded as the first commercially available computer?
questions.solution: UNIVAC-I (1951) was the first computer produced and sold commercially. ENIAC was a one-off military project; EDVAC was a stored-program research machine; IBM 360 is a 3rd-generation family (1964).
questions.shortcut: UNIVAC = the first computer you could BUY; ENIAC = the first one ever BUILT electronically.

questions.q: The correct sequence of steps in a single machine cycle is:
questions.solution: The CPU first Fetches the instruction from memory, Decodes it in the control unit, Executes it in the ALU, and Stores the result.
questions.shortcut: Fat Dogs Eat Snacks: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store. Any option starting with Decode/Execute is out.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

One who is present everywhere at the same time
questions.solution: Omni = all + present → **omnipresent**. The omni-triplet: -potent (power), -scient (knowledge), -present (place) — the stem names the dimension.
questions.shortcut: Omni- family: match the ending to the stem's dimension (place → present).

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Part 1 feels odd ('had' with no participle?) but the no-sooner frame is right so far. Part 2 breaks the rule: after *had* the participle must follow — **the results had been declared**. Convict by rule, not by feel.
questions.shortcut: No sooner had + subject + been + participle.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Needed meaning: misplace → **lose**. *Loose* means 'not tight' and *loosen* means 'make less tight' — neither fits.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Neither…nor → the nearer subject decides: *his assistants* is plural → **were available**. Part 3 followed the distant 'collector' instead.

questions.q: Which river is known to cross the Tropic of Cancer twice?
questions.solution: The **Mahi** rises in the Vindhyas of Madhya Pradesh, flows north into Rajasthan, turns back south-west through Gujarat and enters the **Gulf of Khambhat** — crossing the **Tropic of Cancer twice**.

questions.q: With which neighbouring country does India share its longest international land border?
questions.solution: India's border with **Bangladesh** is about **4,096.7 km** — the longest. China (3,488 km) and Pakistan (3,323 km) follow. The shortest is with Afghanistan (106 km).
questions.shortcut: 'Big Cats Prowl Near My Big Area' — B first.

questions.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution: The **liver** is the largest gland (and largest internal organ). It secretes bile, stores glycogen and detoxifies substances. The pituitary is the 'master gland', not the largest.

questions.q: **Garba**, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2023, is a dance form of —
questions.solution: **Garba of Gujarat** is performed around a lamp (*garbo*) during Navratri. It became India's 15th ICH element in December 2023.

questions.q: If $a + b = 7$ and $ab = 12$, find the value of $a^3 + b^3$.
questions.shortcut: Check: the numbers are 3 and 4, and $27 + 64 = 91$ ✓.

questions.q: What is the HCF of 72 and 120?
questions.solution:
$72 = 2^3 \times 3^2$, $120 = 2^3 \times 3 \times 5$.
Common primes with lowest powers: $2^3 \times 3 = 24$.
questions.shortcut: Both divide by 24: $72 = 3 \times 24$, $120 = 5 \times 24$; nothing bigger does.

questions.q: A cycle bought for ₹850 is sold for ₹1,020. The profit per cent is:
If $\frac{a+b}{a-b} = \frac{7}{5}$, then $a : b$ equals:
questions.solution: By componendo and dividendo: $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{7 + 5}{7 - 5} = \frac{12}{2} = 6$ → $a : b = 6 : 1$.

questions.q: A club's three sports sections show: **15 members in badminton only, 10 in tennis only, 8 in chess only, 6 in badminton and tennis only, 5 in tennis and chess only, 4 in badminton and chess only, and 2 in all three.** How many members play **at least one** of the three sports?
questions.solution: The seven regions are disjoint — add them: 15+10+8+6+5+4+2 = **50**.
questions.shortcut: When every region is given 'only'-style, no formula — just add.

questions.q: How many rectangles (squares included) are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 70 70" width="70" height="70" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="5" y2="65"/><line x1="25" y1="5" x2="25" y2="65"/><line x1="45" y1="5" x2="45" y2="65"/><line x1="65" y1="5" x2="65" y2="65"/><line x1="5" y1="5" x2="65" y2="5"/><line x1="5" y1="25" x2="65" y2="25"/><line x1="5" y1="45" x2="65" y2="45"/><line x1="5" y1="65" x2="65" y2="65"/></svg>
questions.solution: Vertical lines = 4, horizontal lines = 4. A rectangle is fixed by choosing 2 of each: C(4, 2) × C(4, 2) = 6 × 6 = **36**.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PAPER** is written as **KZKVI**. Which word is written as **XLOW** in that code?
questions.solution: P(16)+K(11) = 27 → opposite letters. Opposites undo themselves: X↔C, L↔O, O↔L, W↔D → **COLD**.
questions.shortcut: Decode opposites with the same table — no subtraction needed.

questions.q: **An office is 4 km South of a mall, and the mall is 3 km East of a park. How far and in which direction is the office from the park?**
questions.solution: Park at the origin: mall = (3 E, 0), office = (3 E, 4 S). Gap = $\sqrt{9+16}$ = 5 km, direction (3 E, 4 S) → **South-East**.
questions.shortcut: Stack the offsets in order, then read the pair (number + word) as one answer.
